column1: What's Your Hidden Wound?
column5: The Abandonment Wound | The Rejection Wound | The Betrayal Wound | The Not-Enough Wound | The Injustice Wound
column6: Names the specific core wound running quietly under your reactions, then offers the verse that speaks to it; 'hidden wound / what is my core wound' is a heavily searched self-discovery hook
column8: Inner-child content (Cleveland Clinic, Healthline 'heal your inner child') frames wounds as abandonment/rejection/shame; Christian 'allow God to heal the hidden wounds' devotionals use this exact phrasing

column1: Do You Have Church Hurt? (The Honest Test)
column5: Carrying Real Church Hurt | A Spirit of Offense, Not Abuse | Survived Spiritual Abuse | Mostly Healed, a Few Triggers Left
column6: Settles the question people quietly ask after leaving a church, with grace and zero shame; sits directly on top of proven 'religious trauma quiz' search demand
column8: Multiple ranking quizzes ('Religious Trauma Test', '#1 Religious Trauma Quiz for Christian Women Ready to Heal'); YouTube 'church hurt vs spiritual abuse' and 'spiritual abuse vs a spirit of offense' videos

column1: What's Your Church-Hurt Recovery Stage?
column5: Still in the Fog | Naming What Happened | Setting Boundaries | Grieving the Loss | Cautiously Rebuilding Trust
column6: Maps where you actually are in healing so the chaos has a name and a next step; recovery-stage framing is exactly how the top articles structure the journey
column8: Center for Action and Contemplation 'guide to healing church hurt', Sandstone Care '9 signs of religious trauma & how to heal', Crosswalk '6 healthy ways to recover from church trauma' all lay out staged recovery

column1: Who Do You Need to Forgive?
column5: A Parent | A Former Friend | A Church or Pastor | An Ex | Yourself | God (Honestly)
column6: Surfaces the name your heart already whispered and gently points to the first step; 'who do I need to forgive' is the universal gut-punch question
column8: 'Forgiving someone who isn't sorry' is a top Christian search across iBelieve, Desiring God; forgiveness content repeatedly names parents, exes, church leaders, and self as the hardest targets

column1: What's Fueling Your Bitterness?
column5: An Unhealed Injustice | A Grudge You Keep Rehearsing | Comparison and Envy | Disappointment With God | An Apology That Never Came
column6: Diagnoses the root feeding the resentment so you can pull it instead of fighting the fruit; bitterness as a 'prison you build' is a viral framing
column8: Desiring God 'we cannot cling to bitterness and God', Christianity Today 'how to deal with bitterness and resentment'; CPTSD Foundation '6 ways to let go of resentment' names rehearsed grudges

column1: Can You Forgive Someone Who Isn't Sorry?
column5: You're Ready to Release It | You're Confusing Forgiveness With Reconciliation | You're Waiting on an Apology That May Never Come | You've Forgiven but the Wound Still Aches
column6: Tackles the single most-searched forgiveness question head-on and separates forgiveness from reconciliation; instantly shareable for anyone stuck
column8: Huge search cluster: Psalmlog, Bible Boulevard, Deb Preston, iBelieve all titled 'how to forgive someone who isn't sorry'; central teaching is forgiveness without an apology and boundaries intact

column1: Which Wounded-but-Healed Bible Figure Are You?
column5: Joseph (Betrayed, Then Restored) | Naomi (Bitter, Then Renamed) | The Bleeding Woman (Suffering, Then Touched) | Mephibosheth (Crippled, Then Seated at the Table) | Paul (The Persecutor Made Apostle) | Hagar (Cast Out, Seen by God)
column6: The flagship archetype for the whole cluster: maps your specific wound-to-healing arc onto a named figure who limped out the other side; hope plus honesty in one badge
column8: Strong source base on each: Joseph forgiving his brothers (Genesis 50), the bleeding woman 'so much more than physical healing', Mephibosheth seated at David's table, Naomi's 'call me Mara'

column1: What's Your Triggered Reaction Style?
column5: The Shutdown (Freeze) | The Snap (Fight) | The Vanish (Flight) | The People-Please (Fawn) | The Spiral (Overthink)
column6: Names how your old wound hijacks you in the moment, then shows the gentler response God offers; trigger/fight-flight-freeze-fawn content is massively shared
column8: Inner-child sources (Tim Fletcher, Positive Psychology) explain triggers as 'wounded inner child reacting'; 'why do I get triggered' is a high-volume search with fight/flight/freeze/fawn vocabulary

column1: What Lie Did Your Wound Teach You?
column5: 'I'm Too Much' | 'I'm Not Enough' | 'It's Not Safe to Trust' | 'It's All My Fault' | 'I Have to Earn Love'
column6: Exposes the childhood lie still steering you and pairs it with the truth that breaks it; the 'identify the lie, find the scripture' method is a core inner-healing practice
column8: Christian inner-healing teaching: 'identify every lie from childhood, find scripture that refutes it, meditate on it daily'; lies like 'not enough / unsafe to trust' dominate inner-child recovery content

column1: Why Can't You Trust Church Again?
column5: A Leader Abused Their Power | You Were Shamed for Asking Questions | Community Turned on You | You Saw Behind the Curtain | You're Just Not Ready Yet
column6: Validates the wall you put up and reframes slow trust as wisdom, not weakness; 'can't go back to church' is a raw, relatable confession
column8: Biblical Counseling Coalition 'learning to trust again after church hurt' (trust built on evidence of the Spirit, not time); 9Marks and F. Remy Diederich on the 'walking wounded' misreading new churches

column1: Are You Ready to Find a New Church?
column4: finding a church after leaving one
column5: Heal First, Don't Rush | Ready to Visit but Stay on the Edges | Ready to Try Belonging Again | You Don't Owe Anyone a Timeline
column6: Answers the loaded 'should I go back?' question with permission to go slow; church-shopping-after-hurt is a defined, searched need
column8: F. Remy Diederich 'I left my toxic church, now what?' (grieve the loss first), SOLA Network and YMI 'left the church hurt and came back' on easing back in slowly

column1: Which Toxic Church Pattern Did You Survive?
column5: The Control Culture | The Celebrity Pastor | The Shame Machine | The Us-vs-Them Bubble | The Spiritual Bypassing
column6: Helps you name the exact unhealthy system you escaped, which is itself a documented first step to healing; high recognition, very shareable
column8: Sandstone Care and CAC list high-control environments, shame, and identity-suppression as marks of spiritual abuse; 'name what happened to you' is cited as the validating first step

column1: Which Bible Figure Was Wounded by Religious Leaders Like You?
column5: The Man Born Blind (Cast Out of the Synagogue) | Jeremiah (Persecuted by the Priests) | David (Hunted by God's Anointed King) | Hannah (Shamed at the Temple Door) | Jesus Himself (Rejected by the Religious Establishment)
column6: Tells the church-hurt crowd that Scripture's own heroes were wounded by religious power, and Jesus most of all; validating, surprising, deeply shareable
column8: John 9 man born blind 'thrown out', Jeremiah beaten by priest Pashhur, David fleeing Saul, Hannah judged by Eli, and Jesus rejected by the Pharisees ground the church-hurt experience biblically

column1: What's Keeping You Stuck in Unforgiveness?
column5: You Think Forgiving Means It Was Okay | You're Protecting Yourself From More Hurt | You're Waiting for Them to Pay | Forgiving Feels Like Losing
column6: Diagnoses the belief jamming the lock on forgiveness; reframes the myths that keep people imprisoned in resentment
column8: Mayo Clinic 'letting go of grudges', Renovare 'release resentment'; Christian teaching that unforgiveness 'gives your offender ongoing power' and is a self-built prison

column1: Which Bible Figure's Grudge Are You Carrying?
column5: Jonah (Resentful That Mercy Was Given) | The Older Brother (Bitter at the Father's Grace) | Cain (Festering Jealousy) | Esau (Robbed and Out for Revenge) | Saul (Threatened, Hunting the Innocent)
column6: Holds up a mirror by matching your grudge to a figure who nursed the same one, with a knowing tone and a way out; deeply relatable and tag-a-friend material
column8: Jonah angry at Nineveh's mercy, the prodigal's older brother, Cain and Abel, Esau's vow against Jacob, Saul's jealous pursuit of David are the Bible's classic grudge studies

column1: Which Source of Your Anger Runs Deepest?
column5: Hurt Pretending to Be Anger | Injustice You Witnessed | Boundaries People Crossed | Fear Wearing an Angry Mask | Grief You Never Got to Feel
column6: Reframes anger as a messenger pointing to a deeper wound, defusing shame and inviting healing; 'anger is a secondary emotion' is a viral therapy concept
column8: Letting-go-of-anger content (Centerstone, Headspace) frames anger as covering hurt/fear/grief; Christian teaching to feel anger as a 'God-given emotion' after loss supports the reframe

column1: Is It Conviction or Is It Shame?
column5: Healthy Conviction From God | Toxic Shame From People | A Tangled Mix | An Old Voice That Isn't God's
column6: Separates the Spirit's gentle conviction from the crushing shame religious trauma leaves behind; a genuine lightbulb-moment quiz
column8: Religious-trauma sources name 'persistent shame, guilt, worthlessness' as core symptoms; distinguishing conviction from shame is a recurring church-hurt healing theme

column1: What's Your Path Back to God After Church Hurt?
column5: Through Honest Lament | Through a Safe Small Community | Through Rediscovering Jesus Apart From Religion | Through Therapy and Time | Still Finding the Door
column6: Offers hopeful, non-pushy routes back to faith for people whose connection to God was poisoned by people; deeply saveable
column8: CAC and APA (2025) on rebuilding a spiritual life after religion; recurring theme that 'God was not absent even when people failed' and lament doesn't offend God

column1: Which Bible Figure's Betrayal Feels Like Yours?
column5: Joseph (Betrayed by Family) | David (Betrayed by Absalom, His Son) | Jesus (Betrayed by a Close Friend) | Job (Failed by His Friends) | Hannah (Provoked by a Rival)
column6: Matches the shape of your betrayal to a figure who lived it, so you feel less alone; betrayal stories are emotionally charged and screenshot-ready
column8: Joseph sold by brothers, Absalom's revolt, Judas's kiss, Job's friends, Peninnah provoking Hannah are the go-to betrayal narratives; 'God meant it for good' anchors the hope

column1: Are You Healing or Just Avoiding?
column5: Truly Healing | Numbing and Calling It Peace | Spiritually Bypassing the Pain | Stuck but Honest About It
column6: A gentle gut-check that distinguishes real healing from spiritual bypassing; the provocative either/or drives shares and self-reflection
column8: Recovery sources warn against 'spiritual bypassing' and numbing; Christian teaching that 'God validates pain before He heals it' counters pretending you're fine

column1: What's Your Inner-Healing Next Step?
column5: Name the Wound | Grieve and Lament It | Forgive the One Who Caused It | Replace the Lie With Truth | Invite God Into the Memory
column6: A practical recommender that hands you the one move that fits where you are; turns a vague 'I want to heal' into a concrete step
column8: Christian inner-healing frameworks: honest lament, inviting God into unexplored memories, forgiveness, and lie-to-truth replacement are the recurring named steps

column1: Which Part of You Still Needs Healing?
column5: The Anxious Child | The Angry Protector | The People-Pleaser | The Perfectionist | The One Who Went Numb
column6: Externalizes the wounded 'part' that runs the show, making painful self-knowledge feel safe and tender; parts language is highly shareable
column8: Inner-child / parts-work content (light candle 'for the wounded and judgmental parts of oneself') and IFS-style framing of protective parts is widespread in trauma-healing material

column1: How Bitter Have You Become? (Be Honest)
column5: Barely a Seed | A Root Taking Hold | A Wall Around Your Heart | Bitterness Is Driving Now
column6: A brave, mirror-like self-assessment with a redemptive off-ramp; the 'be honest' framing invites confession and sharing
column8: 'Root of bitterness' (Hebrews 12:15) imagery; Desiring God and Christianity Today frame bitterness as a hardening that 'pulls us away from the Lord' if left unchecked

column1: Are You Angry at God? (And Is That Okay?)
column5: Yes, and You're Hiding It | Yes, and You're Wrestling Honestly | More Disappointed Than Angry | Numb and Distant Right Now
column6: Gives permission for the taboo emotion most believers won't admit, with the reassurance that lament is biblical; rare, brave, intensely shareable
column8: Christian healing content repeatedly normalizes anger at God through honest lament (the Psalms, Job); 'is it a sin to be angry at God' is a recurring, emotionally loaded search

column1: Which Bible Figure Hid Their Wound Like You Do?
column5: Elijah (Ran and Isolated in the Cave) | Mephibosheth (Hid in Lo-Debar, Sure He Was Worthless) | Hagar (Fled to the Wilderness) | Peter (Hid in Shame After Denying Jesus) | Naomi (Came Home Empty and Renamed Herself Bitter)
column6: Names the armor you wear since the wound by matching it to a figure who hid theirs, then shows how God came looking; self-protection patterns are deeply relatable post-hurt
column8: Elijah's burnout cave, Mephibosheth hiding in Lo-Debar believing he was a 'dead dog', Hagar fleeing, Peter's shame, Naomi 'call me Mara'; in each, God pursues the one in hiding

column1: Could You Sit at the Table With Someone Who Hurt You?
column5: Yes, You're Ready | Only With Boundaries | Not Yet, and That's Okay | You Could Forgive but Not Reconcile
column6: Uses the Mephibosheth-at-the-table image to test where you are on reconciliation versus forgiveness; vivid and emotionally resonant
column8: Mephibosheth seated at David's table as a redemption image; forgiveness-vs-reconciliation teaching (you can forgive while keeping boundaries) is central to the forgiveness search cluster

column1: What's the Real Reason You Left the Church?
column5: A Leader Hurt You | The Hypocrisy Broke You | You Were Never Allowed to Doubt | Burnout and Exhaustion | You Drifted More Than You Decided
column6: Helps people articulate the layered 'why' behind walking away, which is the start of processing it; high-recognition, confessional hook
column8: APA (2025) 'rebuilding life after organized religion', YouTube church-hurt testimonies; spiritual exhaustion and 'not allowed to question' are repeated reasons in leaving-church narratives

column1: Which Healing Encounter With Jesus Is Yours?
column5: The Bleeding Woman (Reached Out in Desperation) | The Invalid at Bethesda ('Do You Want to Get Well?') | The Woman Caught in Sin (Released From Shame) | Bartimaeus (Cried Out for Mercy) | The Leper (Untouchable, Then Touched)
column6: Maps you to the Gospel healing scene that mirrors your story and gives you Jesus' exact words to you; comforting, gospel-centered, eminently screenshot-worthy
column8: Gospel healing encounters: the bleeding woman 'your faith has healed you', Bethesda 'do you want to get well?', the woman caught in adultery, blind Bartimaeus, the cleansed leper; hope-forward and saveable

column1: Which Faith-Deconstruction Stage Are You In?
column5: The First Cracks | Angry and Questioning Everything | Sifting What's Real From What Was Control | Quietly Rebuilding | Reconstructed, on Your Own Terms
column6: Names where you are in the messy faith-shift after church hurt without judgment; deconstruction is a high-volume, identity-defining conversation
column8: r/religioustrauma and deconstruction content frame a staged journey (questioning, anger, sifting, rebuilding); APA covers rebuilding meaning after leaving high-control religion

column1: How Well Do You Know the Bible's Wounded Healers?
column5: New to These Stories | You Know the Famous Ones | Wounded-Healer Scholar | You Live in These Stories
column6: A lighter knowledge quiz so the cluster isn't all profiles, riding the wounded-but-healed theme; low-pressure but still on-emotion
column8: Rich material: Joseph, Naomi, the bleeding woman, Mephibosheth, Paul, Hagar, Job, David all carry well-documented wound-to-restoration arcs that make strong quiz questions
